documents.title: MACN REPORTED INCIDENTS - QUARTERLY REPORT 2020 Q3
USA FEDERAL COFR 2022
documents.contentText:
To SSML Teams 

 Cc SSML – managed Fleet ( bcc) 

 Good-day 

 
 A US Federal COFR is required for ships that call, or are likely to call, US ports. 
 

 The COFR is issued subject to there being in place , valid underlying ship’s P&I insurance for oil pollution, and a further top-up insurance purchased from a specialist insurer, each ship. 

 We purchase this specialist cover through SIGCO . 

 
 SIGCO cover premium is offered in two options: 
 

 Full Trading cover : for ships certain to call US ports. 100% full premium is payable . 

 Partial Service cover : for ships that may call US ports. A lower deposit premium only, is payable. 

 Fully-paid ships , are published by the USCG NPFC on its website , with their COFR and VIN no, respectively. 

 Part-paid ships are not shown. 

 For a part-premium paid ship, if it is ordered to the US , SIGCO then upgrades the part deposit to full trading premium, to obtain the COFR . ( see item 6 below) 

 
 The US Federal COFR is issued for a 3-year period , but this is provided the underlying insurances as stated in item 1, get renewed. 
 

 The ship’s P&I and SIGCO insurances are however , issued with a 1-year validity only. 

 Therefore, it is important we ensure that the underlying insurances are kept valid. 

 
 ‘Seaspan Ship Management Ltd’ is named as the ‘applicant’ and the vessel ‘operator’ for the COFR. 
 

 This is for simplicity. 

 Note: the definition of ‘operator’ under COFR is different from that in commercial circles. 

 
 The SIGCO insurance for your vessel COFR, has been renewed for one year from 01 July 2022, but only if the vsl is trading (or likely) to the US - as follows : 
 

 Full Trading cover 

 ONE Parana 

 ONE Magdalena 

 

 Partial cover (deposit) – a standby list 

 CMA CGM Tuticorin 

 CMA CGM Mumbai 

 CMA CGM Mundra 

 

 
 Any ship not named in the list under item 5 “Full Trading cover”, and which receives orders to trade to the US , should immediately notify this office .

documents.title: 2022 MARINE STANDARDS ROVING TEAM MEETING WITH INGENIUM
documents.contentText:
MEETING POINTS OF DISCUSSION AT MUMBAI BETWEEN INGENIUM AND MARINE STANDARDS ROVING AUDITOR TEAM 

 
 Steering test - Guidelines provided in the procedures are ambiguous and interpreted in various ways by the ship staff. Recommend that a detailed extent of the test is specified for arrival so that vessels can follow the same in a uniform manner . The scope of the test could be in close similarity with the USCG requirements so that vessels are familiar with the process when arriving in US ports. 
 Main Engine Test : Noted that some vessels are following the procedure, however for vessels calling ports with congested waters or vessels with time constraints to keep to the ETA , tend to test the engines only from one location. Recommend that either vessels test from all 3 areas outside confined waters or the procedure for testing from all 3 locations is relaxed giving the ship master’s more leeway especially when in congested waters . Suggest that the test from local control be extended as testing from all 3 locations ( local control included ) is time consuming. 
 The importance of the use of Radar equipment on sea stabilized mode to be emphasized with the ship staff mainly for navigation in open coastal waters and open sea. 
 Glitches in One-Ocean Passage planning software in the areas such as 
 

 
 During voyage planning, software does not suggest all the required ENC for the voyage. It only shows ENC which have valid permits. Selecting specific folio would open up all the ENCs. 
 Appropriate ENCS for the passage not included in the ENC list at times and ENC list columns incomplete at times. The NTM to which the ENCs are corrected is not mentioned. Instead, a message " No updates collected" is at times visible. 
 Radio contacts and NAVTEX stations not evident / incorrect. 
 Tidal data not available for certain ports. 
 Arrival and departure port information does not contain important details such as maximum dimensions permitted for the port and safe periods for transit. In the case of certain ports most of the port specific information is missing. 
 One Ocean to be contacted in regard to the instances when minimum depth and CATZOC values in the passage plan can be manually changed and these instructions to be passed to Masters. 
 

 
 T and P plotting : Distance from the charted track where in T and P should be manually plotted to be clearly established in the ECDIS procedures. Plotting of T and P in lieu of solely activating the AIO to be done. 
 Port specific information from Sailing directions and from other sources to be included in the passage plan. 
 Procedure to be established on the required sections of the passage plan which are to be mandatorily included. There is no uniformity among the submitted plans. Many vessels submit passage plans with the AIO information, NAVAREA Warnings, MARPOL, Port specific information, Passage plan notes (1 st page of the plan) and weather information sections of the plan missing. 
 Masters to be reminded that when berthing times are changed, UKC calculations to be revisited and it is to be re-ascertained if company UKC requirements will be complied with. In these circumstances an amendment to the passage plan is required to show continued compliance with company UKC requirements. 
 From the investigations conducted -a focus area which needs improvement is the Master pilot information exchange and a discussion of the berthing / unberthing maneuver. This will prevent over dependence on the pilot and ensure that the bridge team is aware of the maneuver and will be ready to challenge the pilot if/ when things go wrong.

Procedure: Shipboard Management Committee 

 Purpose 

 To provide guidance to Ship and Shore personnel on how to organize and run the Shipboard Management Committee

 
 Scope 

 This applies to all ships managed by Seaspan Ship Management Ltd.

 
 

 Responsibility 

 The Master is responsible to implement this procedure.

 
 

 Procedure 

 Note: The Shipboard Management Committee consists of:

Master - Chairman

Chief Engineer - Member 

Chief Officer - Member

Second Engineer - Member

Electrical Officer - Member 

 Functionality 

 Review the working of the “health, safety and environment committee’ to ensure resources are well utilized.

 Caution! Do not combine this meeting with any other meeting 

 Meet at least once every month with the following agenda:

 Any outstanding action items since the last meeting?

I CLAN – PORTAL FOR VDR PLAYBACK, NAVIGATION AUDITS AND ASSESSMENTS 

 
 Scope of Service and functionality offered 
 

 1) Easy play back using log in and credentials, web based portal through a secure internet connection. 

 2) VDR data playback available as per 

 
 Equipment data captured in VDR 
 Audio (processed for improvement in sound quality) 
 CCTV ( if available) 
 Parameter Graphs and dials 
 Analytics from observations made on checklist 
 Repository for all supporting documents 
 Playback on maps, ENC from NOAA, with integration on pay per view with ENC tiles 
 

 3) Easy play back for reviews and briefing 

 4) User access to ships, fleets as per company roles and responsibilities 

 5) On - line checklist for VDR audits with references to company SMS, and other industry references 

 6) Online report viewing and creation. 

 7) Ability to Benchmark trends across companies if agreed to share information on finding frequencies as per the standard BPG checklist 

 

 
 Terms and Conditions 
 

 

 
 Period: The service is contracted for a period of 12 months 
 

 

 
 Data Processing: Upon receipt of the VDR data from the vessel, VDR information will be played back using the maker software, and extraction of data will be done. Subject to VDR manufacturer software providing a raw data extract dump. 
 

 

 
 Availability on Portal : VDR Data would be processed into the portal and made available in 2 working days from the time complete data is received and verified to be complete. Detailed analytics uploaded within 5 working days from time of commencing the audit. (if audit services included in scope of services Ingenium) 
 

 

 
 Data Storage: Would be stored on cloud server retained for the duration of the AMC , for CCTV the same would be maintained for a period of 3 months. All data shall be stored in Secure Google Cloud and Azure environment. Such data will be governed by the NDA and confidentiality agreement with the client. 
 

 

 
 User Access: Access to Ingenium i -CLAN possible only by creation of users and assigning credentials, passwords, fleets and specific vessels . Allocation can be by Fleets to enable easy viewing and of assigned ships 
 

 

 
 Support: Support for access to Ingenium Portal and data related queries will be through standard email support as per working hours, working days in India. (GMT+5.5) 
 

 

 
 Tax: All fees/amounts mentioned exclude any applicable taxes, and other charges that may apply. 
 

 

 
 Commercials : Access to i CLAN portal shall be charged as follows:- 
 

 

 Annual Subscription and AMC fee – 10,000 USD per year , 

 4 free VDR data uploads included in Annual AMC , thereafter charged at 300 USD per audit. 

 Where Ingenium is performing the detailed audit or investigation, VDR processing fee is waived . 

 Annual subscription includes 10 users log ins . A dditional user s r equired to be discussed . 

 The fees shall be subject to revi sion after 6 months should the number of data calls/playbacks exceed 50 per day. 

 

 

 Ingenium Marine ME FZCO Seaspan Shipping Limited

documents.contentText:
Seaspan Ship Management Ltd. – ISO 14001: 2015 Management Review 

 Date conducted: 1 st Dec 2020 

 a) Status of previous actions from management reviews 

 i) Observations reported during Office Internal Audit conducted in May 2020, were closed within the stipulated time frame. 

 ii) The NS5 (Company Planned Maintenance and HSQE management platform) was superseded by a new FMS (Fleet Management Software). Though platform offers enhanced interface from previous version, the system capability to generate data for analysis of environmental impacts is still under study. 

 b) Changes in: 

 1. internal/external inputs, 

 Environmental Aspects database is maintained as an active document which is updated for any new environmental risks. 

 

 2. Interested parties, 

 SP-619 highligh ts various interested parti es and their environmental relation to Seaspan Ship Management Ltd. The document was reviewed and content found apt. 

 

 3. Significant aspects 

 With the IMO’s focus (MEPC 75 outcome) on reduction of GHG, one of the significant area of development would be to strengthen vessel SEEMP. A joint work group (ESG Workgroup) has been formed with stakeholders representing key departments. The ESG workgroup is expected to define sustainability targets by the Q1/2021. The ISO 14K Targets and Objectives will be reviewed to align with the Company ESG targets. 

 

 4. Risks and opportunities 

 F ormation of ESG workgrou p and drive towards sustainable development will offer ample opportunities for streamlining processes and focused environmental objectives. With ever evolving regulatory framework both international and regi onal, it is important to keep track of the developments to avoid risk of non-compliance. 

 In addition to updates being available through Company DOCMAP, our vessels also have access to Regulatory information through third party software (Regs4Ships) and more recently the ability to introduce geo-fencing in the Enviro-manager will enable overlaying Company requirements in addition to regional and international regulations. 

 

 c) The extent to which environmental objectives have been achieved 

 We have set up six environmental targets and all but one have been met till date . 

 

 d) Seaspan Ship Management Ltd. environmental performance 

 

 1. Non-conformities, 

 NIL 

 

 2. Monitoring & measuring results, 

 Objectives and targets are monitored on a monthly basis and uploaded on DOCMAP. The latest update will be available on DOCMAP 

 There is a 2 - month period to work on the ‘root cause’ and ‘preventative corrective action’. M onitored by Marine Standards. 

 

 3. Fulfil ment of compliance obligations 

 

 Less than 20% of all foreign flagged vessels that operate in US meet strict eligibility criteria for QUALSHIP-21 certification by USCG. This year 31 vessels from our fleet which called ports in USA, qualified and attained certification. 

 MARPOL violations have not been a cause of detention in our fleet and no incident 

 

 4. Audit results 

 Office Internal Audit: May 2020 

 Non-Conformities: NIL 

 Observations: 4 nos. 

 Noteworthy comments: 1 no. 

 Recommendations: 5 nos. 

 

 Shipboard Audits – 39 (Nov 2020) 

 The findings from shipboard audits are to be analyzed and presented during the annual management review. 

 

 e) Adequacy of resources 

 There are adequate resources in all departments to meet the needs of the ISO 14001:2015 standard. 

 

 f) Relevant communication from interested parties including complaints 

 Seas pan received an Honorable mention for 2020 Admiral William M. Benkart , Marine Environment Protection Award for Excellence from the United States Coast Guard. documents.contentText:
Familiarization: DF Equipment – PaNox Marine Selective Catalytic Reduction Unit for Himsen 8H35DF Engines 

 Introduction & Concept : 

 The Selective Catalytic Reduction ( SCR) unit is needed in order to regulate the NOx contents of the exhaust gas emissions from the Diesel generator engines . 

 The SCR is put into use when the engines operate on MGO/ fossil fuel and mostly in port . SCR is not required when the engine operated on LNG. 

 

 Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) selectively removes the oxides of nitrogen (NOx) in the exhaust gases from stationery engines in the presence of a catalyst using ammonia (NH3) as a reduction agent. By chemical reaction, this system produces harmless, nitrogen (N2) and water vapor (H2O), which are discharged into the ambient air. 

 

 

 The ammonia is injected and mixed with the flue gas prior to entering the catalyst react or which is installed in the uptake . 

 An overvi ew of the installation is as shown in the picture above . 

 There is one unit installed for each generator on board, so there are four units on board this vessel. 

 The operation is via a touch screen HMI and in auto mode. Once the start button is pressed, t he system will automatically start in a pre - programmed start up sequence. 

 Main Components of one SCR unit are as follows: 

 
 SCR Reactor with Catalyst 
 Integrated Dosing Unit: this will fulfill needs of all four units . 
 Urea Injector 
 Mixer 
 SCR Control Panel : T his is a centralized control for all 4 SCR . 
 

 The quantity of urea injected is based on the following factors: 

 
 Q uantity of exhaust gas generated by the engine at each load point . 
 

 
 T he exhaust gas temperature at that load. 
 T he pressure loss over the entire process at different loads. 
 

 A Brief Description of the Components is as follows: 

 SCR Reactor with Catalyst 

 The SCR catalyst is the key material of SCR system. The catalyst is composed of the various active materials for the De-NOx reaction. NOx in combustion flue gas reacts on the catalyst surface with injected ammonia. 

 The elements are bundled with the stainless-steel frame . One frame is referred to as a Module . This allows easy handling of the SCR catalyst for transportation and installation in the reactor. 

 Urea Dosing Unit 

 Th e Urea Dosing Unit is the system for feeding the ammonia at the upstream of SCR catalyst. The aqueous urea flow-is controlled by the demand signal at the PLC of the control panel. The PLC’s demand signal is determined by the table of Engine’s load signal vs. a required reagent flow rate. It is injected into the SCR inlet duct through the ammonia injection nozzle. Aqueous urea is converted to ammonia vapor and HNCO (iso-cyanic acid) in exhaust gas duct after engine before the catalyst. Mechanism of urea decomposition is described in the next section.
